utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Morning, all. For the Prosecution, I'm Tom Hannis with Indah Susanti.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic, appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Aleksandar Aleksic on behalf of Mr. Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. While the witness is on his way in, the Chamber wishes to merely note that it is in receipt of what it is intituled "Prosecution and Defence joint motion to file stipulated facts." We wonder about the choice of the word "motion" but we note it as a filing, and I don't think that it -- save for commenting that we are in receipt of it, no further action by the Chamber is necessary. Thank you. We thank counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And, again, for the record, we sit under Rule 15 bis. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, good morning to you. As Mr. Hannis prepares to wind up, I give you the usual reminder as to your solemn declaration. Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, in 1992, did you personally participate in any interrogations of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, did you not hear my question? Did you, in 1992, personally participate in any interrogation of prisoners? I'll try one more time. In 1992, Mr. Macar, did you personally participate in the interrogation of any prisoners? We'll try another set. Good morning, sir. Can you hear me now? Or are hearing interpretation? Now, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. My first question was: In 1992, sir, did you participate personally in the interrogation of any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you in the room when interrogations were conducted by other members of the RS MUP?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps in August, when we did the Yellow Wasps case, I may have passed by their office to see what they were up to. Now the sound in my headset is a little too strong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Too loud? We'll try and push the volume down for you. Now, how's that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fantastic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You don't recall participating or being present during interviews of certain Muslim policemen that had been taken prisoners early in the war, say, April or May; and these interviews would have taken place in Pale?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not as far as I remember. As I said, having arrived in Pale, they went straight to Vrace, to the ministry HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you about -- one question about the Yellow Wasps. That investigation revealed information about Mr. Dusko or Dusan Vuckovic, also known as Repic, you were aware, weren't you, that Mr. Repic said after one of his first killing sprees at Celopek Dom, after beatings and tortures and killings of several Muslim men at Celopek, that he and the reserve policemen who were guarding those prisoners had four of the survivors load the dead bodies on a truck, take them away to be dumped in a pit, and that the reserve policemen then shot and killed the remaining Muslims who had loaded the bodies on the truck. That was information you knew about in August 1992, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, I said it right the first time around. Jurisdiction over the -- over that particular task and jurisdiction over the investigation of Repic, and so on and so forth, was something that was done to the military police, the military prosecutor and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand that, but you're not answering my question. Did you have that information that reserve police had been involved in killing some of those Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can we have, Mr. Hannis, the reference for your claim that this is in the -- in the statement of Repic and to whom this statement was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's in Exhibit P1539. I'll show that to the witness in a minute, but right now, I want to know if he recalls having that information. Tab 31 of the Prosecution's list.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if you ever heard about that, about reserve police having killed some of the prisoners from Celopek Dom in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that. As a matter of principle, the military police and the military security men would not send us any feedback, and I can't remember. I'd like to see that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In a moment. But, if reserve policemen had killed civilian prisoners, that would have been a matter that was subject for police jurisdiction, investigation, and prosecution in civilian court; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegations would need to be checked and verified by civilian bodies. Based on any information received, there would be a verification procedure to ascertain the accuracy of the allegations and that's what the procedure dictated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if, in the course of investigating a crime, the police came across information that the perpetrators were VRS, military personnel, you would have forwarded that information to the military police; right? That was standard procedure, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever information was obtained by the ministry suggesting that a military conscript committed a crime, the military police or the military prosecutor would be informed, sometimes with a delay. Perhaps you'll remember when we talked about 1992, when the military prosecutors' offices were established and when touring the various units and institutions, the administration's inspectors would give instructions whenever such information was obtained to forward the information to the relevant military prosecutors. The distance sometimes exceeding several hundred metres between the place the information was obtained and the relevant military prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I'll show you Exhibit P1539 now in fairness to you. It is an Official Note of the interview with Mr. -- with Repic, Mr. Vuckovic. And it was taken by the military police. It's dated the 4th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the last page in both the English and B/C/S, first of all, just to get the name ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have a hard copy, please. This is very difficult for me to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't have a hard copy with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have the hard copy if ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could have the last page of English in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You see the statement was taken by Lieutenant Milan Stankovic, as I recall. Did you -- did you know him? Do you remember him being there to help with the processing of the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that person. As I said, the military police would receive and assess information, obtained probably from other bodies too, and they would act on that. They handled cases that concerned components or members of the military forces that committed crimes --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You've said that --

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- throughout Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You've told us about that before. So you're saying Lieutenant Stankovic and the military police never shared this information with the MUP? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: "No. Yes." Does that mean you're saying they did not share the information with you? You're sure of that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm 100 percent certain that they did not share this information with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Or anyone else in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is a question for, for instance, Mr. Stankovic and his senior officers. I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you think of any reason why the military police would not want to inform your organ about the allegation that reserve policemen had killed civilians? Generally speaking, weren't the police all too -- weren't the military authorities all too happy to advise you whenever they came across a policeman involved in a crime?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't speculate --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- what the reason might be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you looked at the crime police files and archives, you would, no doubt, realise that there was precious little information that we ever obtained from the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we have some documents that talk about how much information was shared in evidence. We'll look at those. Did you know a Goran Sehovac who, as I understand it, I think was the chief of the Ilidza SJB at some point in time, in perhaps late 1992? Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Mr. Sehovac, I can't remember when, in the middle of the war or sometime towards the end of the war, and after the war. That's when I met him a little better.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you not hear about the event in Kula police station in Sarajevo where he discharged his weapon during, I think, some sort of party or celebration, and killed a -- another Serb named Vlado Vidacak?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to be reminded of the time-period. I do remember, and I remember that this happened. I don't remember any details, though. I know that the Sarajevo CSB checked the circumstances of the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. I believe it was mid-October 1992. Did you know that Tomo Kovac, Simo Tusevljak, Drago Borovcanin, Zoran Cvijetic were all present when this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you know dispatch was sent to the Minister Stanisic the next day to advise him of the circumstances of that event?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't speculate with any precision. I don't know if a dispatch was sent to the minister. As for the event itself, I don't know if I knew about it right there and then, in 1992, or early 1993. I can't be very specific in my speculation. I know there was an investigation and the preliminary steps were taken by the Sarajevo CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: On the face, sounds like a more serious violation than Mr. Andan's poker machine. Were you aware if Mr. Sehovac was ever disciplined or removed from the service or criminally prosecuted for that event; do you know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If memory serves, did he? But I think it was in that sense. I'd like to be reminded and see some documents. I think the investigation, the steps that were taken by the CSB, established that the weapon was used in self-defence. I'd like to see some documents to be able to establish a time-frame for myself, but I think it was in that context that the report was produced by the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, I don't have any --

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is based on my memory. Just to be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand. Do you know a Tomo Macar? I believe he worked for a while as the police chief in -- or deputy police chief in Janja, which is near Bijeljina. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tomo Macar was with the Bijeljina CSB. As far as I know, after the war, he was assistant commander of the uniformed component of the Janja police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you aware that he was arrested in, I think, March of 2009 in connection with allegations of abuse of position dealing with an investigation about the issuing of forged personal documents with an emphasis on links to helping hide people indicted by this Tribunal? Did you hear about that in 2009 or later?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read about it in the media, but any details should probably be provided by the RS Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: He's originally from Sokolac, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where's he from?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He lived in Han Pijesak and Sarajevo, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if that means anything. I am myself from Sokolac. I knew many persons there named Macar. I still do. He is from the branch of the Macar family that straddles the border between Han Pijesak and Sokolac municipalities. Just for your information, it's a century-old family living in the areas of Nevesinje and Tjentiste. There used to be some in Gorazde but there are none around now, as well as Pale, Sokolac and Han Pijesak. The first time the family occurs in written documents in the Dubrovnik state archive dates back to 1274 [as interpreted]. I was just showing my daughter that book the other day and I was actually quite jealous because actually the Stanisic family name occurs in 1373 which is a full year before my family name occurs in written documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, speaking of relations between Macars and Stanisics, isn't Tomo Macar a brother-in-law of Mico Stanisic? You know Mr. Stanisic very well. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mr. Stanisic from my professional life. But I don't really know him all that well personally. His habit, as well as mine, was not to mix business and private life.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. But can you answer my question.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as for -- I'll answer your question. As far as Mr. Tomo Macar is concerned, I met him in 1993, when --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, please. Please Mr. Macar.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I explain, please, when I found out about --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My question is: Do you know that Tomo Macar is a brother-in-law of Mico Stanisic? That's a yes or no question.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out in 1993 that Tomo Macar was Mico Stanisic's brother-in-law. And I had never realised that any of the Macar family were close relations to Mico Stanisic. Not ever, until 1993, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the rest, Mr. Tomo Macar and I are no close relations. I met him only in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you about another Macar that you are related to. Zoran Macar is your brother; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. He is a year and a half my senior.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in 1992 and 1993, he worked for the Sokolac police; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No? Where did he work?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In 1992, Zoran Macar was a member of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, he spent seven months with the Ministry of the Interior in the crime prevention administration, specifically in the anti- sabotage unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you know a Miro Seslija who dealt with a -- explosives in the RS MUP?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Miro Seslija was head of the anti-sabotage unit. He wasn't into explosives, not during his time with the MUP. He was dealing with anti-sabotage activities. As for the rest, and please feel free to ask, I know The Hague investigators spoke to my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. How about Brano Mandic, cousin to Momcilo Mandic, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brano Mandic was an employee of the Ministry of the Interior, even before the war broke out. He was also involved in anti-sabotage work. As to the degree of kinship between the two persons you specified I don't know about that. I don't think he ever pointed out the existence of any family links between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about a Sretan Forkan [phoen] who worked in the Foca police, did he also deal with anti-sabotage?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he worked for a while in the Sarajevo centre. I'm not sure if it was anti-sabotage work, or whatever. And I can't remember what became of him later.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that he was often used. The anti-sabotage mostly dealt with anti-sabotage work as it related to buildings, facilities and the safety of persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 90 per cent of their work was about securing the Assembly building, the government buildings, and certain other institutions. They weren't working with explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. One more person and then one question about the whole group. Sredo Vucenovic, nicknamed Terrorist, did you know him? Apparently from Banja Luka police. Did he also work with anti-sabotage?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vucenovic worked in the anti-sabotage unit. In the former MUP there would be anti-sabotage units in all of the local organisations, and the same applied to the crime prevention administration. And for a while, too, the state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And isn't it a fact that you were involved in having these men come to Bijeljina and they actually blew up five mosques in March 1993? Would you like some more water?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honourable Judges, this question, I believe, is -- I won't say it is disrespectful or anything like that, but I did suggest to the Prosecutor to freely address me because ... I know about information that I received in Bijeljina. The worst of it is the fact that this information was conveyed to me by a former member of the Ministry of the Interior in a drunken state. I don't think it's a problem for me to name him in public. Mr. Ostoja Minic. He was drunk when he told me -- this may entail the use of some foul language. Perhaps you would like me to quote him, perhaps in closed session or I might as well say it like that. He said I fucked their mother --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, please. My question was: Did you --

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you do this? You can say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, it's a ridiculous question. It's ridiculous to establish any link between me and somebody like that or indeed anyone from the anti-sabotage unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: One of the persons I linked you to is --

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know for a fact that five mosques were destroyed in Bijeljina in March 1993? That did happen, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Macar, let us continue where Mr. Hannis broke off. The demolition of these five mosques, your role in that in 1993. So tell me, we heard that you confirmed that these events did happen. As far as you know, was that ever investigated?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was investigated. The public security station and the public security centre took operative measures. They went to the crime sites, and I believe that they even wanted to consult about the means used. It was a task of the SJB and the CJB to collect information about the events; namely, the demolition of the mosques. And I would like to amend my previous answer. The MUP was not in possession of explosive devices. I do not quite remember what was found, what was used to demolish the mosques. Was it military explosive or industrial explosive? We'd have to consult the materials from the centre. At any rate, I know that the SJB and the CJB investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, I kindly ask you to be clear. You can't say anything like "the gentleman I have mentioned" because you have mentioned dozens of people. That's no way to answer questions. Please tell me the following: The CSB in Bijeljina, or the MUP, did they have any information about the involvement of any of these persons, or your involvement, in the events in connection with the demolition of the mosques in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was that established in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no indications that pointed to the involvement of any MUP member from SJB level up to headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that the source of that information was Ostoja Minic, who was -- told you that when he was drunk?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in a pub. He said that he had spoken to ICTY investigators and that he said to them in the interview that Goran Macar, administration chief, chief of the crime enforcement administration, had brought his brother to -- his brother, or relative, to the administration, who allegedly was trained to work with explosive devices, and with that relative and other anti-sabotage personnel, organised the demolition of the Bijeljina mosques. I think that this can be corroborated if his interview given to the investigators can be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify one thing. It was recorded here that Ostoja Minic told you that. Did he tell you or did you hear it from somebody else saying that he was saying that when he was drunk in a pub?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me directly. I received information that he was drunk and spoke about that in a Bijeljina pub.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But please be mindful of the need to make a pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all right. But you must understand that this is very irritating and quite unbelievable.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, on the first day of your examination, Mr. Hannis asked you a couple of questions. The page reference is 23119. He asked you about Predrag Jesuric and Malko Koroman. In the context of your conversation with Jesuric about Mico Davidovic, tell me, please, when did -- or when was Predrag Jesuric appointed SJB chief? Was it before April 1992 or after that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If memory serves, he was appointed before April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was Malko Koroman chief of Pale SJB before the 1st of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Malko Koroman was in that position before. I believe that he replaced Vlastimir Kusmuk, who retired or -- anyway he ceased to be station chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If Malko Koroman and Predrag Jesuric were SJB chiefs before April 1992 in Bijeljina and Pale, who appointed them to their positions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were appointed to their positions by the minister of the interior of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Who was minister?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Alija Delimustafic, but who was minister before him? Immediately before the war, Mr. Alija Delimustafic, whom I knew personally, was minister. And we spoke about the dispatch of the MUP, and I can say something about that to the Prosecutor too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. And the Prosecutor interrupted you. But we'll get there yet. I wanted to give you a chance to give a full answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P648.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 23130, on the first day of your testimony - and I'm afraid you don't have that document in the binder, you can only see it on the screen - the Prosecutor showed you this document. It's from September 1993, and on the last page - that's page 10 - we see the name of Tihomir Glavas in the signature block, who, at the time, was chief of the Ilidza SJB. Do you remember the document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that this is it how I looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me not read the transcript now because I'd have to read in English. It was about the role of Tomo Kovac in the events before the outbreak of the conflict in April 1992. On page 6 of this document, there was a nomination for decorations. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's show the witness page 6. You see that it says "Tomislav Kovac," and the Prosecutor quoted from the document, and you said that you were not familiar with these facts.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The arming of the Serbian people, the organising of illegal work, and so on. The answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, sir -- I would like to show you page 7 as well and item 5 on that page. Kovac is number 1, and we see that item 5 is a nomination of who?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tihomir Glavas. Then followed by Branislav Okuka --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm just interested in Tihomir Glavas. It says here that he was chief of Hadzici SJB. Is this person mentioned in item 5 the same person that signed this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know that there was another name -- another man by that same name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it follows from this that Tihomir Glavas nominated himself to be decorated?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Glavas; and what opinion do you have of him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him superficially and cannot say anything about his character.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To your mind -- no, I can't ask you that because it would be calling for speculation. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 21.261 of the 12th of July, 2011, a document was shown to you. It's a dispatch by Mr. Mandic; P353. Do tell us, because we have some three minutes left, tell us briefly, because Mr. Hannis interrupted you when you started talking about Mr. Delimustafic. You said on that page: "I had the opportunity to spend some time with Mr. Delimustafic in mid-March 1992." And then Mr. Hannis said: "No, no. Please stop. That's not the answer to my question."

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to be as fast as possible. I've known Alija Delimustafic for many years, from a time before the war. In my statement I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I need to interject at this point. This is not something I believe that was listed in the witness's 65 ter statement or his proofing statement. And now it's coming up for the first time in re-direct when I'm not going to have any opportunity to deal with it. So I would either ask that it not be permitted or I be given the opportunity to address it in re-cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't in -- in a proofing note or 65 ter list because I wasn't aware of -- of this fact until Mr. Hannis brought the subject in his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I didn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Hannis. And then the witness said -- then the witness said: "Let me tell you, but I would like to tell you, Your Honours, that sometime in mid-March, I had an opportunity to spend some time with Mr. Delimustafic, and" -- And then Mr. Hannis: "Well, I'm sorry. Let me stop you there. That's not an answer to my question. That was not something that was informed in your 65 ter or proofing note, as far as I know. It is not something that I want to go into at the moment. Perhaps Mr. Zecevic or the Judges may ask you about it." And that is a precisely what I'm doing. I am asking about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's my point, Your Honour. It was not an answer to my question. So I didn't elicit it, he volunteered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. But, nevertheless, it appears it was an expansion - unwanted by you - in terms of a question that you asked, and it appears to be something that is not irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The choice of the double negative is deliberate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Though then I understand I should be given an opportunity to re-cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If -- if -- if that appears necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. We return in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the witness is ushered in, I have an oral application to make. I informed the Registry about it. At transcript page 14.938, it was agreed that the Zvornik municipal -- Municipality Zvornik municipal bulletin currently on Defence list as 654D1 be added to the law library. However, the parties omitted to put it in our law library filing and we are applying now that this document be assigned exhibit number. In addition, the parties have agreed to apply -- to ask the Trial Chamber that, besides the first document, 654D1, two more Zvornik bulletins, 656D1 and 663D1, be added to the law library. And in addition, the parties agreed that 1D181 MFI, be added also to the law library, and, therefore, de-MFI'd. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it from what you would have said that this is an agreed position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So -- so ordered.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, therefore, exhibit numbers assigned will be L333, L334, and L335. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And just for the record, the 1D181 will be de-MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand either -- either way is preferable. There is no preference from the Registry's point of view, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Macar, could you please finish your previous answer.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four or five days after the 15th of March, the day known as the day the command of the 2nd Army District in Sarajevo was laid siege to, I went to the Cenex company owned by Alija Delimustafic and his brothers. I was on my way there to hand over the money that was due, proceeds from my family shop run by my brother and my parents at Sokolac. I got some of my supplies from that company for our family shop. At the entrance to their offices, and I think that was sometime in the morning, between 9.00 and 10.00 in the morning that day, I met Alija Delimustafic. He invited me to his office. I wanted to explain to him briefly the reason for my visit. I said 32.000 German marks had arrived to be used to pay for the previously delivered merchandise. Normally payments would be postponed, and this amounted to about 16.000 euro. He looked at me, he lowered his bag, or briefcase, and asked me to come with him to another room in a different part of the building. It was like a club room that he used for meeting his business partners. There were perhaps four or five chairs there around a table. The first thing I noticed was that he ordered a whiskey, and that was the first time I ever saw him order hard liquor like that. When the drinks arrived, he raised a toast to me and he said, Goran, don't pay. I remember his words very well. This will all go down the drain. My people have decided to press the issue to the bitter end. At first, I was confused by his offer to not pay. At the time, you would have been able to buy two Golf passenger vehicles for that kind of money. At the same time, his remark reverberated in my head, what he said about everything going down the drain and his people pressing the issue to the bitter end, or taking the issue to the bitter end. Confused as I was, I asked him, Alija -- because that's how I normally addressed him. We were neighbours in Marin Dvor and I had known him for quite a number of years. I said, Alija, can you please explain this? Because he really gave the impression of being very worried. He looked very worried. And he said, Goran, can't you see what's going on? And he listed all sorts of different things. First he talked about the army district command case and the inability to relay tensions in the ministry itself or, indeed, on the ground. To be perfectly frank, I was confused. There were some other comments that were made, but, eventually I answered. Alija, you know, and I think I used this word, if there is trouble, even that will, one day, be over, and we might continue to work together afterwards, after the trouble is over. I said, Neither my brother nor I can agree to this non-payment proposal. I handed over to him an envelope containing some German marks and some dinars. We were using the currency exchange rate that was used on the black market and whenever you bought something, it would always be converted like that, according to that rate. And we parted in some confusion, I do remember that, and all I can say is that I haven't seen him since.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, at page 21261, the Prosecutor showed you P2320. This is Prosecution tab 79. And we should soon have it on our screens. Mr. Hannis asked you the following question: "You will agree that Mr. Delimustafic and the collegium wanted to stop this process and were calling on all members of the MUP to go back to work and to perform their regular duties as of no later than the 2nd of April?" And then your answer. Sir, I think we talked about this. After the review at Sokolac on the 30th of March, did you go back to the BH MUP to go on performing your routine duties there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you continue to work as usual until the 3rd of April?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would go to work every day, as usual, until the 3rd of April. And if I may just add one thing, briefly, something that I was trying to tell Mr. Hannis, even this dispatch signed by the collegium does not invalidate Mr. Mandic's previous dispatch. Not that I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The fact remains the dispatch in front of us right now was signed by Mandic; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that's his signature. I don't remember exactly what it looked like, but it certainly looks like it might be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the header of the document there is a reference to dispatch UZSK, number 2, dated the 23rd -- the 31st of March, 1992. It's a dispatch number 022482 and that's a dispatch sent by Mandic on the 31st of March. Do you agree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Zecevic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Page 23187. You were shown 1D46.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have that on our screens. Thank you. This is OTP tab 104.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: An order dated the 15th of May, 1992 - could we please go to page 2 of the document - signed by Mico Stanisic, Minister of the Interior. Do you recognise Mr. Stanisic's signature there, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The same page, 23187, you were asked by Mr. Hannis: "Do you know whether this staff ever met? Did it ever start operating in 1992?" And you said: "I think this body never operated." And Mr. Hannis asked you the following question: "At least you didn't go to any meeting convened by this staff; right?" And you answered: "That's true, I didn't." And then it goes on like that. Sir, did anyone at the MUP HQ ever tell you that a meeting of this staff had been held?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. No one of told me that a meeting had been held or, indeed, that anyone had attended a meeting of this staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see any decisions or orders signed by a body like that called the staff?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P530, the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis wanted you to comment on it. This is 23225 of the LiveNote. He asked you specifically about -- my apologies. I can't find the reference at this point in time. It was about Mr. Hannis's question. I'll have to read this in the English just to make sure everything is complete. [In English] "Mr. Hannis: Okay. Thank you. Now could you look at the phrase for me and tell me what you understand that to mean, because it says: "'... regulations passed by the municipal assembly and relating to the law and order and road safety ...' "And then it says: "'... as well as other regulation in the domain of internal affairs ...' "What does that mean? Can you give me an example of regulation that would be in the domain of internal affairs that doesn't relate to law and order and road safety?" Your answer: "Well, I can't really recall and I don't want to speculate?" [Interpretation] You remember that particular exchange with Mr. Hannis, don't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you know that -- do you know whether in some municipalities in the territory of the former Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia regulations were passed about bans on pouring alcoholic drinks in catering establishments anywhere throughout that territory?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That included certain regulations concerning the business hours of these catering establishments as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that municipal assemblies passed certain regulations banning the consumption of alcoholic beverages before 11.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 11.00 was just by way of an example. It could have been a different point in time. But it was about banning the sales of alcoholic beverages before a certain time in the day.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were regulations that were passed about the procedures applied in catering establishments while conducting business, but there were regulations like that that applied to rallies and public meetings being held as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am being told that this is Article 27, which is page 4 of the law. What about the following regulation: A regulation imposing a speed limit in a settlement or a village because of the vicinity of a school or a creche? Can that be considered to be part of the same regulations under Article 27?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As well as sounding your horn, for example, near a school, a hospital, or a creche.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I've used that example already, so I might just rehash it for the present purpose. Visegrad municipality, for example, adopts a decision to protect the old bridge across the Drina River. For that purpose, they decide to ban all traffic across the bridge, or perhaps to ban heavy vehicles from using the bridge. Would that also be an example of regulations under Article 27?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Be that as it may, but did members of the Ministry of the Interior, based on such regulations, have a responsibility to act in compliance with these regulations?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, if there was a municipal regulation adopted on a municipal level that ran counter to the letter of the law, in a case like that, would the Ministry of the Interior still have to act in compliance with that regulation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only would it be under no obligation to implement something like that, but it would not have the authority to do that, as long as the regulation in question ran counter to any existing law that applied at the time throughout the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 22899 is the page reference in the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a verification request there. 23230 is the next reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just to clarify one thing. Mr. Hannis asked you a question there over the total number of CSB heads and we know that there were five: Trebinje, Doboj, Sarajevo, Banja Luka, and Bijeljina. So over that number, do you know how many of those were appointed by the minister in 1992? And you say: "He probably appointed all those heads himself. Their personal files should reflect the fact that he either signed the relevant decisions or not." Mr. Macar, tell me, please, out of these five, Trebinje, Doboj, Sarajevo, Banja Luka, and Bijeljina, which CSBs existed before the 1st of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Banja Luka centre and the Doboj centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the names of the chiefs of these centres in Banja Luka and Doboj before the 1st of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Bjelosevic and Mr. Zupljanin were chiefs there before the 1st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's move onto a topic that Mr. Hannis devoted a lot of attention to in his cross-examination. Page -- it begins on page 23235. It has to do with war crimes committed against ethnic Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at two documents first. Could the witness be shown 961D1, which is tab 7 in the OTP binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a form of the decision, an -- an empty form that has a signature and a seal. Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 1D91, which is Defence tab 111.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, please look at these documents before you now. First, there's a text of an order, and then there's a handwritten text, and there are two signatures. Whose signatures are these?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic's, the first one; and I believe the second one as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now please look at P173, tab 13. This is a document shown to you by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page 2, please. I'm particularly interested in the signature at the bottom of that page in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, earlier we saw some signatures that you were able to recognise. Do you recognise this signature; and, if so, whose is it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This, too, is the signature of Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 1D635, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also showed this document to you. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then Mr. Hannis asked you about this document, and you discussed it.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The question of Mr. Hannis was ... So Mr. Hannis asked you about whether you knew why you would be duty-bound to provide information to the Federal Secretariat of the Interior. Do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just show you P181, which is tab 112; Article 3 of the constitution. Tab 112.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We're waiting for it to appear on the screen. Sir, this is the text of the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina from the Official Gazette. Article 1 says: "The Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is a state of Serbian people and citizens living therein." Would you please read out Article 3 of the constitution?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the English text as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. "The Republic is a part of the federal state of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does this pertain to Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because this is the constitution of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, we will now go back to the document which had been shown to you, P173, tab 113 of the Prosecution. We just saw that document earlier. It speaks of war crimes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel repeat the number of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P173; page 2, please, which is the Prosecution tab 13. Page 23235, and then 236, 7, and 8 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you remember that you spent quite a lot of time discussing this document with Mr. Hannis and discussing war crimes committed against members of the Serb nation.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then, in a part of your answer, you said that there was a campaign, a visible campaign, against ethnic Serbs in the media and that this is why they insisted on making sure that this material is documented and presented.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Presented in the public and provided to certain organs, in order to be presented to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now tell me, sir, in that period of time, in 1992, or at least in mid-1992, because this document is from May of 1992, the cases of crimes where the Serbs were victims, were they treated different by the media than the crimes where the victims came from other ethnic communities?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, as far as you know from the media, was it typical for all cases of crimes against Serbs to be doubted in the media? Did the media express doubts about it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The media, outside of Bosnia and Herzegovina, either didn't report on this, or if the victims were, indeed, Serbs, it was portrayed in the media as a crime against some other ethnic community. I remember that there was a case where a crime was committed somewhere near the Drina River, and there was a picture of a mother holding the skull of her son. And I remember that in some media, it was portrayed as a crime against non-Serb victims, and the expression of pain was quite palpable. I remember that particular case. And in most cases, there was no information whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that fact, in your view, did it affect and did it have anything to do with this document, where they ask that the crimes against Serbs be documented in every possible way, in great detail?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that that was also one of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown, please, P1977, which is tab 109 in the Defence binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have for you the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this document has 11 pages, and on the last page, we see the typed text, "Dr. Radovan Karadzic, President of the Presidency." The document has not been signed, but on the first page, it says: "Pursuant to Article 7.5 of the Law on Defence and pursuant to the proposal of the cabinet of the government, the President hereby adopts guide-lines on tasks, modes of action and functioning of defence forces of state organs and subjects, in the field of economy and social activities in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in the state of war." Tell me, please, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember some things from this document, but I don't know for sure when I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document includes guide-lines for work in the areas of defence, internal affairs, judiciary, and public administration, finance, the economy, social work, foreign policy, and others. These are nine separate chapters in all. Let us take a look at page 3 and item 7 on that page. The subheading reads: "Defence-related tasks." It says: "The Ministry of Defence in co-operation with the Main Staff and the commands and units of the army will solve manning of the units continuously, as -- as well as materiel and technical supplies, for the army, importing young soldiers into the registers, recruitment pursuant to the needs of the army, referring the young recruits to training centres," et cetera. Mr. Macar, do you remember that the Ministry of Defence acted pursuant to this guide-line in 1992 or later?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. And it was the only body that had remit over these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us turn to the following page. I'm interested in item 9 under the subheading: "Tasks in the field of internal affairs." Item 9 reads: "The minister of the internal affairs should adjust its war-time structure to the needs and tasks in war-time conditions ..." And then there is a list of activities: Public law and order, traffic, and so on. All these matters are specified by law. Did the ministry act in accordance with these guide-lines?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. Only it had an additional obligation, and that is resubordination to the Army of the RS for purposes of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We'll get there yet. We're now talking about the first paragraph of item 9. These things listed here, such as public law and order, traffic control, physical protection, intelligence and counter-intelligence, the protection and control of border crossings, issuing of identity documents, and so on, all these things that the ministry was tasked with, was that done in keeping with the Law on Internal Affairs of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of this item, item 9, we read that the minister of internal affairs shall adopt a special enactment on the internal structure of the Ministry of Internal Affairs in war-time conditions, and so on. So tell me, sir, we saw a document dated 15 May about the establishment of the MUP staff of which you said that it never really operated, that you never heard anyone say that it did, nor that you attended any meeting of that body. For the sake of reference, that's 1D46. When it is said here that the minister of internal affairs shall adopt a special enactment, could that be this document that I have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible. But I don't know that this document was implemented, but it may refer to these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the last paragraph of item 9 reads: "Both active and reserve police, as well as members of units for special tasks, which are not part of the war-time structure of the ministry ... will be placed at the disposal of the army units or -- or assigned to other war-time tasks."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, we started a little later, so you can go for another five minutes or so if the witness is able to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must repeat the question, sir. Does this paragraph, 3, is this what you spoke about when you were amending your answer about the first question pertaining to this item?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be as precise as to say that I was referring to this language. But, as far as I remember, I spoke about the need that, in case of combat operations and resubordination of the police, the police should act as an organised unit rather than as individuals that were assigned to the army. And I also explained that what could not be covered by the existing organisation had to be resubordinated to the army because we wouldn't have been able to account for the surplus.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Item 10, which is the second item on this page of the document; that's page 5, and I'm interested in the second paragraph of item 10, which also spells out the tasks of the Ministry of the Interior. It reads: "The Ministry of Internal Affairs and its organisational elements shall collect and process the data and material on ... crimes committed and genocide of the civilian population." Sir, this task of the MUP, was it carried out?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The MUP documented war crimes committed against the civilian population without distinguishing on the basis of ethnicity, to the extent it had any information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The following subheading reads: "Tasks in the field of judiciary and public administration." And item 13 says: "The judiciary bodies of the state shall closely cooperate with military judiciary bodies, especially with regard to status issues of prisoners of labour," it says here "... and detained persons, then to collecting information and evidence for the initiation of procedure -- proceedings against the perpetrators of crimes and genocidal actions, as well as ... other issues of collecting evidence," and so on, "whether they are military or civilian perpetrators." Sir, can you comment on this task that the president gave the Ministry of Justice?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear the duties of the civilian and military judiciary bodies are very clearly outlined.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the following page, which is page 6, item 13 is repeated, but that is obviously a typo. And we read: "The Ministry of Justice and public administration, in co-operation with the Presidency and the government of the Serbian Republic ... shall intensify the work of the state commission for the establishment of crimes and genocide against the civilian population and victims of war, and the state commission for the exchange of prisoners of war and detained persons, and they shall ... co-operation with international organisations and courts and the organs of the United Nations regarding the scope of work of these commissions." And then it says that international -- the international law of war shall be strictly observed. Can you comment on this item, too?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This item, which should be item 14 [as interpreted] because it follows after 15, it is clearly stated what the state commission for the establishment of crimes is to do. In practice, in many cases they deviated from this task. They also engaged in some activities that were not in their remit. That's why I often had clashes with that commission. I even demanded at meetings that their tasks be even more precisely defined, and I also wanted somebody to tell them that they cannot engage any activities from the remit of the MUP. Especially they were not allowed to conceal any information or documents in order to publish books and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, does this item mention the issue of the ethnicity of the victims or the civilian population as anything relevant?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This item mentions civilian population without distinguishing on ethnic or any other grounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the previous item on page 5, the task given to the Ministry of Justice about -- I believe that this is a typo too. These are not prisoners of labour but prisoners of war and detained persons. Can you comment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, if you're going on to something new, perhaps we could take the break at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So we return in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, item 13, page 5, under heading 4: "Tasks in the field of the judiciary and administration." What specific state organs, based on these guide-lines, did the President of the Presidency confer authority upon in relation to prisoners of war and detainees?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The justice ministry from the RS government who were to cooperate with military courts and prosecutors in taking certain steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What about your own recollection? Does your own recollection suggest that this was, indeed, the case back in 1992, and these bodies were, indeed, dealing with these issues?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Late 1992, I received information about that a month or two or three months later, suggesting that the representatives of the ministry of the RS performed some of the jobs, in terms of gaining insight into the situation in some municipalities and some specific facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, just let's take one thing at a time please. My question was as follows: What about your own recollection? Does your own recollection suggest that that was indeed the case back in 1992 and these bodies, meaning the justice ministry and the military bodies, were, indeed, dealing with these persons or these issues? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the leading form of the question and the fact is he did answer the question when it was first asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I wasn't -- I didn't find that this was the -- the answer to my, I believe, proper question. What is -- what was your recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If memory serves, the justice ministry took certain measures along with the relevant military bodies. I can't be more specific as to what type of contact and, and ... and the mode of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What about the Ministry of the Interior? Were they, too, involved in the contacts between the justice ministry, on the one hand, and the military authorities, on the other, regarding these issues?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that the role of the ministry or anyone from the Ministry of the Interior had anything to do with these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You will remember that - just to move on to something else - that at one point in time you were asked a question about some information that I had previously shown you, and then Mr. Hannis quoted your answer at 22967. It was about the question of vetting personnel in the public security stations and CSBs, and according to your answer, it also had to do with anomalies in certain municipalities where chiefs of public security stations were unable to have proper communication and to make sure the proposed appointments materialised because of obstruction by municipal leaders. Mr. Hannis read your own answer back to you and you said that it had not been properly interpreted. In the meantime we submitted a verification request to establish what you really said, and we established that there was an error in the transcript, which has, in the meantime, been corrected. Your answer to my question was this. I asked you: "Tell me this: This reminding by dispatch the municipality presidents and Executive Board presidents, did that yield any results, and if so, what results, partial, fully successful, or less successful?" And your answer was: "In one part of the municipalities, despite this instruction, not to call it a warning, there were no results. If anything, there was even more obstruction later." Tell me, sir, which municipalities specifically did you have in mind when you said this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, Samac municipality which was available to me based on reports. Prijedor municipality as well, where I had some personal experiences. I also know there was a lot of obstructionism and many attempts to exert undue influence when appointments were made in Bijeljina, specifically the Bijeljina centre. There was a lot of turnover regarding the personnel moving from one area to another. I think back in 1993 there were some attempts to exert pressure on the ministry, specifically from Bijeljina, and you can tell if you look at our working meetings in some of the reports that were later issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just to be as specific as we possibly can, since you're expanding again. We want to know about 1992. In this specific answer, which municipalities were you talking about, in relation to 1992 alone?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can we clarify for the witness that the document is dated the 20th of November, 1992, so in which municipalities after 20 November 1992 was there even greater obstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard the question, sir. Which municipalities were you referring to? The document is dated November 1992. So which specific municipalities were you referring to, but only in relation to 1992.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Samac, above all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What about Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had some direct experience with the station chief. He stated at one point that he had not received any orders from his own superior officers. He told us about this when he took us to have breakfast there. So Prijedor would fall under that. The municipal bosses, the Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I think the record shows that the visit to Prijedor was on the 15th of November, one day after the witness's birthday, and therefore five days before this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just about to ask you the question, sir. You were in Prijedor on the 15th of November. This document is dated the 20th of November. You said that obstruction continued. Based on what do you say that, that obstruction continued after the 20th of November, 1992, as you suggested? I'm talking about Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from my direct personal experience, you asked me about 1992, right? So I told you my direct personal experience of actually going there. I know about the minister's orders to public security stations telling them to keep on vetting their own men. And I know the Banja Luka centre was unable to do that for Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was that in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: After the 20th November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992, yes. I wasn't specifically talking about this November or that November.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Macar, please concentrate. I have had to ask you quite a number of times to try and stay focussed in your answers in order to avoid wasting time. You confirm that after this summons on the 20th of November, obstruction continued in some of the municipalities. My question was which municipalities, and you said Samac and Prijedor. After that, you provided, in relation to Prijedor, the example of your own direct personal experience five days previously, previous to this 20th November mark. We're talking about obstruction that continued from the 20th of November on to the end of December 1992, in the case of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that even after that date the chief of the public security station [as interpreted] still couldn't comply with this order to appoint personnel in keeping with what the centre was proposing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, at page 23254 ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's an error in transcript; 42, line 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you say the chief of the public security station or the chief of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the Banja Luka CSB could not comply because of obstruction with the proposed appointments in Prijedor until the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis asked you about a document there. Was it you, was it a deputy that you had sign some documents on your behalf, and who was authorised to grant approval. I'm talking about the annual report. And you said that was a draft report, and you said you didn't know what final shape that report took. You went on to state: "I said I don't know. At the beginning of that question, in relation to the very beginning of your question, I don't know if anything was changed, if any changes were made to the document or not. This is a draft document. I don't know if anyone entered any changes or not. That would constitute mere speculation. "The Trial Chamber had an opportunity yesterday to see for themselves, based on a document that I produced, that we were able to check the crime police archives. I wanted to prepare myself," and so on and so forth. And you go on to say: "Regrettably I have to inform the Trial Chamber that the request was not acted upon because the MUP was afraid that someone might be accused of aiding and abetting war criminals." First of all, tell me which document, which year were you referring to when you said: "... yesterday I produced a document to the Trial Chamber ..."?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I showed the Chamber a letter from 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Take it easy, please. This is the letter that you showed us. We all exchanged copies of that document. Is this the letter that you sent to the Ministry of the Interior back in 2005?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the one that I sent to the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Seeking what? Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked to be allowed access to the crime police archive in relation to documents between 1992 and 1995 and a number of other documents that I specified in that letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So back in 2005, did the Ministry of the Interior grant you access to that archive?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't. Of which I duly informed the investigators that I spoke to in Belgrade, showing them the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Which investigators? Whose investigators?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Tribunal's OTP investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, page 23264, you commented on a document, 1D661, that document, at tab 57. If you feel unwell, sir, please let us know immediately, in keeping with the Chamber's instructions and we can have a break. Mr. Hannis asked you some questions about those conclusions. He said: "It seems to me that such conclusions or regulations passed by the Crisis Staff were something that had to do with public law and order. In keeping with Article 27 of the Law on Internal Affairs," as you had occasion to see, "the public security station will be implementing those regulations. "Sir, tell me how this constituted interference with the work of the public security station?" And then you said: "I have no problem with that. The Crisis Staff has a problem with that. There are issues that are regulated under the Law on Public Law and Order and the Law on Criminal Procedure, and those are not under the jurisdiction of the Crisis Staff. That body, the Crisis Staff, has no authority to adopt decisions regarding elements that are already regulated under the law." And then you went on to speak about which law specifically and issues like that. You were asked to provide, if you could, the exact reference as to the exact regulations. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see document P181, please. That is tab 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The document is the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you have it in front of you. The Ministry of the Interior, is it an administrative body at the level of the republic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a centralised body at the level of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Under the Law on Public Administration, do the organs of the republic have the right and the duty to establish their territorial branch offices to exercise their powers?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do. They organised their territorial units at the municipal or at the regional level.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, to which Assembly does the Ministry of the Interior, as a whole, report?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Assembly of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do the organisational units in the municipalities or regions report to another Assembly, with regard to their work?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SJBs report to the Ministry of the Interior for their work, and they can also inform the municipal assembly about some relevant events. But that's merely information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us take the example of the Vlasenica SJB and their work. Who reports to the Assembly about its work, as well as the work of all other stations; and which Assembly is that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the Ministry of the Interior which reports to the Assembly of the RS. It reports about the activities of any station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For reference, the articles of the constitutions are 70 and 144 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let's go back to page 23296. You were shown document 1D644. That was on 14 July. The tab number is 99.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we have a repeat of the articles of the constitution? One of them is listed as 144, which in --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, this is a report on inspection which was shown to you by the Prosecution. He asked you - the Prosecutor - "we have spoken with you about" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down and start again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, the interpreters need you to slow down and start again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
