utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hannis asked you: "We have seen earlier in your testimony your role in the commission that investigated certain activities of Mr. Kljajic and Dragan Andan in Bijeljina, and the disciplinary proceedings against Andan were launched pursuant to the conclusions of that commission. Was any commission established to investigate the work of Mr. Koroman that you have any knowledge about?" And your answer is: "I spent the month of August in Bijeljina, possibly September, too. And then I briefly went to Pale and then returned to Bijeljina, and I cannot say with certainty whether the CSB did anything at all." It continues on page 23298. This is again Mr. Hannis's question: "Mr. Koroman, to say the least, issued weapons. Let me remind you those are the weapons that you spoke about that he gave to members of the Yellow Wasps. I believe that the weapons are listed in the document that we have, and they include automatic weapons and even hand-held rocket-launcher, and nothing happened to him," meaning Mr. Koroman. "Do you degree that this is disproportionate?"

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, that was Mr. Hannis's question. And then, finally, page 23299: "... if Mr. Koroman really issued weapons at the time ..." And your reply: "If Mr. Koroman really issued weapons at the time" -- this seems to have been mistranslated so I'll read it in English. [In English] "If Mr. Koroman did provide weapons at the time when the public security department had information incriminating members of Yellow Wasps, then that is certainly a more serious violation." [Interpretation] Sir, we have seen that Mr. Dragan Andan was sanctioned. Disciplinary proceedings were initiated against him. What was his disciplinary offence; can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The disciplinary offence of Mr. Andan was the use of a device without respecting the procedure that was in place in the ministry. It was not in line with the instruction on the conduct of crime enforcement workers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, was there a criminal offence of unauthorised possession or sale of weapons in the Criminal Code?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Unauthorised trade in weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was there a serious punishment envisaged [Realtime transcript read in error "alleged"] by the then legislation for that offence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that the transcript reads "alleged"; whereas, I said "envisaged," or "stipulated."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, if a -- if it were to be established for a MUP member that he or she gave weapons, what's more automatic weapons, to some persons without authorisation, would that be -- would that person be liable to both disciplinary proceedings and criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us go to the last page of this document, page 6. And it's item 2 of the conclusions of the inspector who drafted the report in March 1992 [as interpreted]. It says: "Once taken from the proposed Pale SJB employees, the statements will have to be analysed for possible elements of crime, the crime administration and the Sarajevo CSB senior officers informed accordingly, and once criminal responsibility has been assessed, criminal reports submitted to the competent prosecutor's office." Do you agree with this conclusion or proposal of this inspector?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This proposal is fair. Once the facts have been established, they're forwarded to the higher authority for -- to act upon and check the allegations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Koroman removed along with the senior officers of the Pale SJB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In what year was the -- were the proceedings for their removal initiated?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we have some clarification on what "removal" means? Removal from the position, or removal from the Ministry of the Interior? Because his previous evidence indicates that Mr. Koroman was still working for the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, my question was precisely, was Mr. Koroman removed along with the senior officers of the Pale SJB. Removed from the Pale SJB. That's ... I wasn't suggesting that he was removed from the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know if the Sarajevo CSB investigated against the senior officers of the Pale SJB, including Mr. Koroman, and if they filed a criminal complaint against anyone?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if a criminal complaint was submitted, but the centre was duty-bound to conduct checks with regard to the allegations in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll move onto another matter. Tell me, sir, do you know anything about the relation between Mr. Kovac and Mr. Trbojevic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If memory serves, they were not very close, nor were they on friendly terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I inquire which portion of my cross-examination this arises from? Can I have a page reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 23305. It's in connection with the document I'm about to show the witness. It's P192. The question was about that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, there's nothing in that document about a conflict with Mr. Trbojevic and Mr. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't talking about a conflict. I merely asked what their relationship was like, if the witness knew anything about that. You'll realise later why I asked that question once we comment on the following document. May the witness please be shown P192, which is OTP tab 86.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just if I can have the instruction at what time should we break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, subject to the witness's disposition, we will see if we could press straight through until the end because we expect that that would permit to you finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I will try, do my best, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, are you ready to press on for another 45 minutes?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, you were shown this document. You remember discussing it with Mr. Hannis; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Page 2, we see Mr. Tomo Kovac's signature. He was assistant minister for police work and tasks. You see that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me how documents of the police duties and tasks administration were marked?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, they used number 3, to mark those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go back to page 1 of this document? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This was sent to the president of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the prime minister of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The date is the 8th of August, 1992. It's marked as 10-239/92. The number 10 there stands for what administration?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The analytics administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, as Mr. Hannis previously told you, the first paragraph of this document shows Mr. Kovac as saying "I propose," and then, at the very end, "I hereby present the problem in this way." Sir, is it usual for positions of the ministry itself to be presented in the first-person singular?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is by no means common. When state bodies exchange letters, unless obviously we are talking about an order, and the ministers would have the authority to order things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This letter was sent to the president of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the prime minister. Sir, there is no reference at all in this letter to a ministry position; rather, as I said, it was written in the first-person singular. Do you remember if the ministry, at one of its collegium meetings, ever considered the issue of classifying arrested persons?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document is dated the 8th of August; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness please be shown P427.13. P427, paragraph 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, these are minutes of the 46th Meeting of the Government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, held on the 9th of August, 1992. It reads -- the 9th of August, that is the date of this document. It reads: "The session was chaired by Milan Trbojevic, deputy prime minister, and goes on to state that the session was also attended by so on and so forth. Tomislav Kovac, on behalf of Mico Stanisic, was standing in for Mico Stanisic. And it says: "The following were absent and excused: Branko Djeric," and other ministers there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's standard procedure as far as minutes such as this document were concerned, relating to government meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At page 3, item paragraph 12, which is the first paragraph there. And the first sentence reads --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be page 4 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These are items on the government meetings agenda. Can you please confirm what paragraph 12 says, one of the items on the agenda of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Agreement including visits to the camps in the Serbian Republic of BiH."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then just in order to move onto paragraph 12, the English there is correct. And this is page 5 of the Serbian. What is the government's conclusion there? You see, it says: "The government set up two commissions comprising representatives of the Ministry of the Interior and the justice ministry and the administration. The objective of the commissions is to gain insight through the relevant state bodies into the status of people in concentration centres and other collection facilities. And also to speed up the procedure of classifying these persons, as well as to establish their responsibility and any punishment to be imposed." Sir, who established these commissions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what it says here, the government established two commissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And what was the task that was given to these two commissions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was given by the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember if, at any collegium meetings back in 1992, you reviewed any reports compiled by any commissions at all, specifically this one?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, and I would have been present. So I'm certain that no such thing occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At page 23325 you were previously shown a document, specifically an order by the minister to disband the special units that had been established during 1992. Mr. Hannis says, I'll read in English: [In English] "And the order to disband special units was not issued because there were some reports about crimes committed by those units or individuals from those units. That was the only -- that was not the only reason." [Interpretation] That's actually part of your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can have I the page reference again. I'm not finding it on page 23235.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hannis goes onto say: "I agree with you that that was perhaps not the only reason. If you agree with me that that was one of the reasons." And then the discussion goes on. Finally, Mr. Hannis's question, a question about -- he was talking about an order by the president of the Presidency and an Assembly decision, so he showed you P199. Please have a look, sir. That's tab 115. An Assembly meeting held between the 24th and 26th of July, 1992. I suppose you don't have a copy of that. That's an OTP document. You'll have to follow the document on your screen, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page 13, which is page 14 in e-court, in the Serbian. The last paragraph, words uttered by Mr. Karadzic, his own contribution at that meeting. Mr. Karadzic says: "One of the fundamental problems" -- that is the last paragraph. I'll try and locate the right reference for the English. Your Honours, I have not prepared the relevant references for the English, and it's a lengthy document. I will be coming back to that later, probably tomorrow, at the start of our day tomorrow. I may have 10 or 15 minutes left for tomorrow, first thing in the morning. And now I'll use something else instead, but I will have a printout of this for you so that you can follow, because the print there is very small.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Page 23329 of the LiveNote, you spoke to Mr. Hannis about Bosanski Samac and the replacement of Stevan Todorovic. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The question was: "Who had the authority to replace the chief of the public security station, like, for example, Mr. Todorovic? Would that have been the head of the CSB or the minister, or both of them?" And then you say at page 23302: "I think I said that the minister transferred some of his powers to the CSB heads, in relation to the proposed appointments for leading positions in the public security stations, meaning the chiefs and other leading men in the stations." And then the key question, Mr. Hannis makes the following suggestion: "In the Law on Internal Affairs there was no provision preventing Mr. Bjelosevic from removing Mr. Todorovic; right? It was a practical problem, a political problem. Political support or public support that existed in Samac but there were no legal obstacles to that." And then you say: "As an economist, I will try to answer that question for you." You remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, what about men in leading positions, such as the head of the CSB? Would these persons have any authority over members of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What about CSB heads? Would they have any authority, in terms of working relations, in terms of disciplining people, over persons working in other state bodies?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if a criminal offence is committed, but no disciplinary action.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, do you know if Stevan Todorovic ever - when I say "ever," I mean 1992 - did Mr. Stevan Todorovic at any point in time throughout 1992 sign a contract to officially work for the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I think one of the reports that followed one of our visits actually reflects that. He was hired by the Crisis Staff and not by the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D518, please. That's our next document. A letter by the centre head, Andrija Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You see that it contains a remark and the document itself is dated 25 November 1992. It's addressed to the minister and says: "We wish to mention that Chief Todorovic never received a decision on assignment to these duties, and it was for this reason that no disciplinary proceedings could be initiated against him." Is this in keeping with the information you had from the reports submitted to the MUP?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then, in this case, if somebody acted as being in a certain position but actually wasn't -- didn't have employment with the MUP at all, did the chief -- did the chief of CSB --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm objecting because this is a leading question. It needs to be phrased in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, is a CSB chief authorised, or has he any authority over persons not employed with the MUP?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He couldn't take any action against them. He could only try to create the pre-conditions for his replacement. And when I say "pre-conditions," I'm referring to the local circles that appointed him so that there should be no problem with appointing somebody else. I don't know if I was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You have already spoken about that. It's recorded. Sir, on page 23403, on the 15th of July, the Yellow Wasps operation was discussed, and Mr. Hannis put this to you: "Isn't it a fact that the leadership of the RS was much more interested in processing crimes such as thefts of Golf cars than in processing any one Serb for crimes against non-Muslims?" And then you replied: "If it's referring to the Yellow Wasps, I don't know what the grounds for your conclusions are." And then, later, Mr. Hannis says: "It turns out that, in spite of your initial information, the subsequent information received from the military prosecutor's office" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, our impression is that the witness is experiencing some discomfort. We are wondering whether we should, inasmuch as we have to return tomorrow in any event, whether we should take the adjournment now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: By all means, Your Honours. It is up to the witness. I informed him that at any time he can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Macar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we continue tomorrow anyway, then, it's all right. And we can take the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So -- so if this is a convenient point, we can take the break now, Mr. Zecevic. Or did you want to finish the question you were --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps if I can just finish this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 23408, let us just finish this. "As the information received from the military prosecutor's office, as opposed to your initial information, pointed to the fact that Vuckovic and other Yellow Wasps were not military persons. And that's why they ought to be prosecuted before civilian courts. Were you aware of that?" And then you say: "This document is dated 14 September. It was not sent to the MUP, and I'm not aware of this." Sir, do you know if a criminal complaint for war crimes eventually was submitted to a court in Serbia against these persons, after all?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know which year that -- that was?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late 1992 or 1993, I don't recall. But I do have information that it was submitted to the relevant bodies in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: How was the jurisdiction of the court in Serbia established in the case against these persons?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been based on their citizenship.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Document 1D86. I just want to show it to you. This is a criminal complaint. You can see the date. Which year is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a criminal report against Dusan Vuckovic, Vojin Vuckovic and other members of the Yellow Wasps for war crimes, as we can read on page 1; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Trial Chamber, the court decision in this case is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat the document reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, the interpreters need you to repeat the reference to the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. P1979. It's the decision of this Court in the case against Vojin and Dusan Vuckovic who were convicted of war crimes. Your Honour, I believe this is a convenient moment for an adjournment. I may have an additional 15 or 20 minutes tomorrow. I'm sorry, I really wasn't able to finish today. I apologise to Mr. Macar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we reconvene tomorrow morning in this courtroom at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
